Fixed and committed as `27ba0d2` on `main`.

**The bug:** `ReconciliationWorker.run` counted every unmatched payment row. A bank retry carries the same payment id, so each copy was counted separately. The fix counts distinct payment ids instead.

Changes:
- `src/orders-api/reconciliation_worker.py`: the unmatched payments are collected as a set of ids, so each id counts once.
- `tests/test_orders_api.py`: new test `test_a_retried_payment_with_the_same_id_counts_once`.

verified: I added the test before the fix. It failed with `AssertionError: 2 != 1`, the reported double count.
verified: After the fix, `python3 -m unittest` from the repo root runs 9 tests, all passing.
verified: Only the tests call `ReconciliationWorker` in this repo. I checked the callers by searching `src` and `tests`.
inferred: The scheduler that runs the nightly job lives outside this repo, so I have not checked what it calls. That is the one caller I could not see.
inferred: Deduplicating by payment id is the right rule. I'm assuming retries share an id and that two different payments never share one.
